threats.affected_asset: User credentials and accounts
threats.scenario: An internet attacker uses credential stuffing or repeated password guesses to take over an account.
threats.preconditions: A valid account identifier is known or guessed and password authentication is reachable.
threats.trust_boundary: Browser to application and authentication/session boundary
threats.evidence_source: The original sequence model explicitly shows repeated failed logins and no lockout; this is design evidence, not source-code verification.
threats.existing_control: The historical model includes credential validation but does not establish throttling or lockout for the affected flow.
threats.planned_or_demonstrated_control: Generic authentication failures, per-account and per-client throttling, temporary lockout, and strong password hashing.
threats.residual_risk: Distributed low-rate attempts and reuse of passwords compromised elsewhere remain possible.
threats.validation_method: Automated login-failure, rate-limit, lockout, and generic-response tests.

threats.affected_asset: Session-protected notes and user identity
threats.scenario: A caller reaches a protected note operation without a valid authenticated session.
threats.preconditions: A protected route omits or incorrectly performs server-side session validation.
threats.evidence_source: The original insecure model includes an unauthenticated notes request; absence of a check in a diagram is not proof of an implementation defect.
threats.existing_control: Token validation is modeled for sync but not consistently for every notes flow.
threats.planned_or_demonstrated_control: Central server-side session validation on every protected route with fail-closed behavior.
threats.residual_risk: Authentication middleware defects or accidentally unprotected future routes remain possible.
threats.validation_method: Unauthenticated access tests for each protected route and route-inventory review.

threats.affected_asset: Opaque session tokens
threats.scenario: A stolen, fixed, replayed, or non-revoked session token is used to impersonate a user.
threats.preconditions: An attacker obtains a token or the application fails to rotate, expire, or revoke it.
threats.trust_boundary: Browser to application and authentication/session boundary
threats.evidence_source: The historical model returns and stores an auth token without documenting storage, rotation, expiry, or revocation properties.
threats.existing_control: The diagram names an auth token but does not establish secure lifecycle controls.
threats.planned_or_demonstrated_control: Opaque random tokens, server-side token hashes, secure cookie attributes, rotation, idle and absolute expiry, and logout revocation.
threats.residual_risk: A token stolen from a compromised browser remains usable until detected, revoked, or expired.
threats.validation_method: Session creation, rotation, idle and absolute expiry, and logout-revocation tests.

threats.affected_asset: Notes, account state, and session state
threats.scenario: A malicious site causes an authenticated browser to submit an unwanted state-changing request.
threats.preconditions: Cookie-authenticated state-changing endpoints accept requests without a valid anti-CSRF token.
threats.evidence_source: The original sequence model contains browser POST and DELETE requests but does not model CSRF validation; this is a review gap, not confirmation.
threats.existing_control: No anti-CSRF property is established by the historical diagram.
threats.planned_or_demonstrated_control: Cryptographically random session-bound CSRF tokens validated on every state-changing browser request.
threats.residual_risk: Cross-site scripting or a compromised browser can bypass token-based CSRF protection.
threats.validation_method: Missing and invalid CSRF-token rejection tests plus valid-token state-changing request tests.

threats.affected_asset: Other users' note titles, bodies, and exports
threats.scenario: A malicious authenticated user changes a note identifier or export request to read or modify another user's data.
threats.preconditions: A data query uses a public note ID without also constraining the authenticated owner ID.
threats.trust_boundary: Authenticated user to application and application to database
threats.evidence_source: The insecure historical model queries all notes and does not model object ownership checks.
threats.existing_control: No object-level authorization is established in the original insecure sequence.
threats.planned_or_demonstrated_control: Owner-scoped database queries for every read, update, delete, list, and export operation.
threats.residual_risk: Authorization regressions in new query paths remain a high-consequence risk.
threats.validation_method: Cross-user read, update, delete, and export denial tests.

threats.affected_asset: Administrator privileges and user administration
threats.scenario: A normal user invokes an administrative operation or changes effective role state.
threats.preconditions: An administrative route trusts client state or omits a server-side role check.
threats.evidence_source: The original model includes administrator actions without showing role enforcement at each action.
threats.existing_control: An Admin actor is named, but actor naming alone is not an authorization control.
threats.planned_or_demonstrated_control: Server-side role checks on all administrative routes with denied-access audit events.
threats.residual_risk: Compromise of a legitimate administrator account still grants intended administrative authority.
threats.validation_method: Normal-user denial and intended-admin success tests.

threats.affected_asset: Browser sessions and rendered note content
threats.scenario: Attacker-controlled note content executes script when stored or reflected into a page.
threats.preconditions: Untrusted text reaches an HTML execution context without context-appropriate escaping.
threats.trust_boundary: Browser to application and application to browser
threats.evidence_source: The historical model notes missing input validation but does not establish an exploitable rendering path.
threats.existing_control: No output-rendering guarantee can be inferred from the sequence model.
threats.planned_or_demonstrated_control: Template autoescaping, text-only rendering, a restrictive content security policy, and no unsafe HTML insertion.
threats.residual_risk: Future rich-text features or unsafe template changes could introduce execution contexts.
threats.validation_method: Stored XSS-shaped payload rendering tests plus template review.

threats.affected_asset: Database records and authentication data
threats.scenario: SQL-shaped attacker input changes a database query rather than being treated as data.
threats.preconditions: Application input is concatenated into SQL or an unsafe raw query.
threats.evidence_source: The historical sequence model does not contain source-level database query evidence, so implementation status requires code review and tests.
threats.existing_control: No source implementation is assessed by the diagram analyzer.
threats.planned_or_demonstrated_control: Parameterized ORM queries, constrained raw-SQL use, and treatment of SQL-shaped strings as ordinary note data.
threats.residual_risk: Future hand-written queries or unsafe migration tooling can reintroduce injection paths.
threats.validation_method: SQL-injection-shaped input tests and static review for query construction.

threats.affected_asset: Note content and browser security context
threats.scenario: Attacker-controlled output is inserted into HTML, CSV, or another active context without safe encoding.
threats.preconditions: A renderer treats untrusted text as markup or fails to encode for the destination context.
threats.trust_boundary: Application to browser and export boundary
threats.evidence_source: The original flow displays notes but does not document output encoding; diagram absence is only a review signal.
threats.existing_control: No output-encoding property is established by the historical sequence diagram.
threats.planned_or_demonstrated_control: Context-appropriate escaping in HTML reports, templates, and exports with no direct untrusted HTML interpolation.
threats.residual_risk: New output formats require their own encoding and formula-injection analysis.
threats.validation_method: Malicious report-field and note-output escaping tests.

threats.affected_asset: Credentials, internal schema, and implementation details
threats.scenario: An error response exposes secrets, database detail, stack traces, or sensitive field names.
threats.preconditions: An attacker can trigger a failure whose internal detail is returned externally.
threats.evidence_source: The original insecure model explicitly returns an error naming a password field and labels it sensitive.
threats.existing_control: The historical insecure flow demonstrates the disclosure rather than a mitigation.
threats.planned_or_demonstrated_control: Generic external errors with correlation IDs and separately protected internal diagnostic logging.
threats.residual_risk: Operational logs can still disclose sensitive context if log fields are not curated.
threats.validation_method: Failure-path tests that reject stack traces, SQL detail, and sensitive values in responses.

threats.affected_asset: Passwords, note bodies, keys, CSRF values, and session tokens
threats.scenario: Sensitive values are written to application or audit logs and exposed to operators or log systems.
threats.preconditions: Logging captures raw requests, secrets, note content, or exception context without redaction.
threats.trust_boundary: Application to monitoring or notification adapter
threats.evidence_source: The archive models security logging but does not prove field-level redaction or a runnable external adapter.
threats.existing_control: Historical logging concepts do not establish what data is logged.
threats.planned_or_demonstrated_control: Structured allow-listed audit fields that exclude passwords, note bodies, keys, tokens, and CSRF values.
threats.residual_risk: Unexpected exception text or future fields can bypass an incomplete redaction policy.
threats.validation_method: Audit-record content tests and logging-field review.

threats.affected_asset: Encrypted notes, password hashes, user identifiers, and audit records
threats.scenario: An attacker with database-file access reads sensitive stored data or alters security state.
threats.preconditions: The database file, backup, or storage volume is copied or exposed.
threats.evidence_source: Database compromise is an explicit repository threat-model assumption; the sequence diagram alone cannot validate storage controls.
threats.existing_control: The historical notes database is named but its at-rest protection is not established.
threats.planned_or_demonstrated_control: Authenticated encryption for note titles and bodies, hardened password hashes, and restricted database-file access.
threats.residual_risk: Metadata, audit records, and password hashes remain exposed; offline password guessing remains possible.
threats.validation_method: SQLite plaintext-absence and cryptographic tests plus documented deployment file-custody review.

threats.affected_asset: Note-encryption master key and decrypted note content
threats.scenario: An attacker obtains or replaces the encryption key and decrypts or corrupts stored notes.
threats.preconditions: Runtime environment configuration, deployment secrets, or host memory is compromised.
threats.evidence_source: The compact reference scope requires an environment-provided key and explicitly excludes production KMS or HSM integration.
threats.existing_control: No production key-management integration is claimed.
threats.planned_or_demonstrated_control: A 32-byte environment-provided key, AES-GCM with unique nonces and associated data, plus key-version metadata.
threats.residual_risk: Host or environment compromise exposes the active key; rotation is operational rather than automated.
threats.validation_method: Configuration validation, nonce/associated-data tests, and documented production key-management review.

threats.affected_asset: Application availability and authentication capacity
threats.scenario: Repeated requests consume CPU, database connections, or endpoint capacity until legitimate work is delayed.
threats.preconditions: An attacker can make sustained requests and controls are absent or only single-keyed.
threats.evidence_source: The historical model explicitly labels an export flow as lacking rate limiting.
threats.existing_control: No distributed infrastructure is present; the original insecure flow documents missing throttling.
threats.planned_or_demonstrated_control: Login-specific per-account and per-client throttles, bounded request bodies, and per-user note quotas in one process.
threats.residual_risk: Database-backed throttle state persists, but check/update serialization is process-local and is not a distributed or edge rate limiter.
threats.validation_method: Login-throttle burst and concurrency tests plus production design review for distributed limiting.

threats.affected_asset: Application memory, request workers, and storage
threats.scenario: An attacker sends an oversized request body that consumes memory, parsing time, or storage.
threats.preconditions: The HTTP stack or application accepts bodies larger than the intended note limits.
threats.evidence_source: Large-body behavior is in the modern threat scope but is not represented by the historical sequence diagram.
threats.existing_control: No request-body limit can be inferred from diagram evidence.
threats.planned_or_demonstrated_control: Reject requests above a documented maximum before expensive parsing or database work.
threats.residual_risk: Upstream servers may buffer bodies before application code sees them.
threats.validation_method: Maximum and oversized request-body tests plus deployment proxy configuration review.

threats.affected_asset: Per-user note storage and database capacity
threats.scenario: A user creates excessive notes or large cumulative content to exhaust storage and degrade queries.
threats.preconditions: An authenticated user can create notes without count, length, or storage constraints.
threats.trust_boundary: Authenticated user to application and application to database
threats.evidence_source: The original flow creates notes without documenting a quota; absence in a sequence diagram is not confirmation.
threats.existing_control: No quota property is established by the historical sequence model.
threats.planned_or_demonstrated_control: Title/body length limits, a per-user note-count quota, bounded pagination, and user-scoped exports.
threats.residual_risk: Many accounts can collectively consume storage; the count quota is application-level and is not a database-enforced atomic quota across multiple workers.
threats.validation_method: Boundary-length, per-user quota, pagination, and export-scope tests.

threats.affected_asset: Audit records and accountability for sensitive actions
threats.scenario: A user or administrator denies a sensitive action and the operator lacks a trustworthy event record.
threats.preconditions: Authentication or note operations are not recorded with actor, action, outcome, and correlation context.
threats.trust_boundary: Application to database or audit adapter
threats.evidence_source: The historical insecure model explicitly labels note creation as having no audit logging.
threats.existing_control: Some historical diagrams mention security logs, but the insecure notes flow explicitly lacks an audit event.
threats.planned_or_demonstrated_control: Structured records for authentication, logout, note changes, export, and denied admin access without sensitive payloads.
threats.residual_risk: Local audit records can be altered by a host or database administrator and are not an external immutable log.
threats.validation_method: Action-to-audit tests and inspection that forbidden secret fields are absent.

threats.affected_asset: Administrator privileges, user data, and audit visibility
threats.scenario: A legitimate or compromised administrator performs excessive access or destructive actions beyond operational need.
threats.preconditions: An administrator account is compromised or administrative authority is too broad and weakly monitored.
threats.trust_boundary: Normal-user to administrative functions and operator boundary
threats.evidence_source: The historical architecture includes an Admin actor with provisioning and security-tool actions but no least-privilege analysis.
threats.existing_control: A distinct Admin actor is modeled; this does not prove least privilege or monitoring.
threats.planned_or_demonstrated_control: Narrow server-side RBAC, explicit administrative routes, and audit events for access and denials.
threats.residual_risk: The demonstration has a simple role model and does not implement approval workflows or privileged-access management.
threats.validation_method: Admin authorization tests, denied-access audit tests, and manual least-privilege review.

threats.affected_asset: Application configuration, cookie policy, debug state, and secrets
threats.scenario: Unsafe configuration enables debug disclosure, insecure cookies, weak limits, or accidental use of development secrets.
threats.preconditions: Deployment accepts missing, malformed, or unsafe environment settings.
threats.evidence_source: Deployment configuration is not represented by the historical sequence model and must be assessed in code and runtime settings.
threats.existing_control: The analyzer makes no claim about deployment configuration state.
threats.planned_or_demonstrated_control: Fail-fast configuration validation, Secure cookies in test and production modes, rejection of non-loopback development or test bindings, no committed real key, and debug disabled.
threats.residual_risk: Operators can still select unsafe settings or expose environment configuration at the host layer.
threats.validation_method: Master-key rejection and production-cookie tests plus deployment checklist review.

threats.affected_asset: Application source, dependencies, build inputs, and runtime integrity
threats.scenario: A compromised dependency or build input executes malicious code or alters security behavior.
threats.preconditions: A trusted package, source input, or build environment is compromised or insufficiently reviewed.
threats.evidence_source: Supply-chain risk is part of the modern repository scope and is not asserted as a historical finding.
threats.existing_control: No production build or dependency-monitoring system is claimed by this portfolio demonstration.
threats.planned_or_demonstrated_control: A bounded dependency list, review of updates, and optional vulnerability scanning when available.
threats.residual_risk: A trusted upstream release or developer environment can still be compromised.
threats.validation_method: Dependency inventory, lock/declaration review, and recorded scanner execution when tools are available.

threats.affected_asset: Note content, exports, identifiers, profile data, and audit records
threats.scenario: Personal data is retained longer than intended, included unnecessarily in exports or logs, or not deleted consistently.
threats.preconditions: Retention rules are undefined, deletion is incomplete, or exports include data beyond the requesting user's scope.
threats.trust_boundary: Application to database and user-scoped export boundary
threats.evidence_source: The archive contains cleanup and export concepts but does not establish a retention policy or verified deletion semantics.
threats.existing_control: A timed cleanup participant exists historically, but its policy and implementation are not verified.
threats.planned_or_demonstrated_control: User-scoped export and deletion behavior, data minimization, and an explicit production retention decision outside the demo scope.
threats.residual_risk: Backups, audit retention, and legal deletion requirements are not implemented by the compact local demonstration.
threats.validation_method: User-scoped export tests, deletion tests, and documented retention-policy review.
